observed.facings.png: Four facings at one scale. South: only two small dark gooseneck hooks side by side, nothing else. East: a steel ladder seen lengthwise. Its two rails angle so they are farther apart at the right end, which carries gooseneck hooks, and closer together at the left end. It has 7 thin vertical rungs. West: a mirror of east with the hooks on the left. North: a ladder seen face-on. Two outer rail posts rise into gooseneck hooks at the top and carry clamp bands. Two inner ladder rails are set slightly inward and converge a little toward the bottom. About 8 thin horizontal rungs are spaced wider at the top and closer together lower down. Dark steel grey with light highlights and a thin dark outline.
observed.south.png: Two small dark grey inverted-U gooseneck tops on a transparent canvas, about 30 px tall, in the lower middle. Nothing else is drawn.
observed.east.png: A lengthwise ladder in the lower right of the canvas. The rail ends at the right curl over as gooseneck hooks. The upper rail slopes down toward the left and the lower rail is nearly level, so the ladder narrows toward the left. 7 thin round rungs with open gaps. Steel grey.
observed.north.png: A face-on ladder in the middle of the canvas. Outer gooseneck stanchion posts carry clamp collars. The inner ladder rails converge slightly downward. Rungs are thin round bars; the top gaps are wide and the lower 4 to 5 rungs sit closer together. A small soft shadow offset shows along the rails. The doubled rails (post plus ladder rail on each side) make each side read as a thick double bar.
observed.west.png: A mirror of east: the hooks are on the left and the ladder narrows toward the right. Same 7 rungs and the same steel palette.
observed.scale.png: An in-pit composite with a human for scale. The north ladder hangs on the north pit wall with its hooks over the rim and its rails reaching down the wall face. The east wall ladder (lowered) has its hooks at the east rim and extends west over the pit. The west ladder (raised) extends past the west edge. At the south rim only the two hooks are visible. The size against the pawn is plausible for a 1.5-cell ladder.
observed.wall_context.png: Panel 1 repeats the scale scene. Panel 2 is the north wall at 2x: the ladder's posts stand on the wall face, the hooks curve over the rim, and the rungs get closer together toward the pit floor. It reads as a fire-escape ladder fixed to the wall. Panel 3 shows the raised state for north and south: the north ladder slides up above the rim with the posts left behind, and the south ladder shows from inside the pit. Panel 4 is the raised north ladder at 2x.
observed.siblings.png: Reference RM_LadderRaised north, south and east. Same thin steel rails, gooseneck hooks and clamp collars, at the same size class and in the same style.

BORE.seen: The gooseneck rail tops are solid bent ends. No open pipe bore shows on any facing.

PORTS.seen: The card lists no code-defined ports, and there are no couplers, hoses or cords.

WALL_LEAN.seen: In wall_context the east ladder's hooks sit on the east rim and the ladder narrows and drops toward the pit (west). The west ladder mirrors it, and the north ladder hangs on the north wall face. Each facing's perspective matches its wall side.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: No code ports, and no drawn connectors besides the gooseneck rail tops, which are part of the ladder, not ports.

LAYERS.seen: In wall_context the north ladder draws over the wall face and the hooks draw over the rim. Nothing that should be behind draws in front.

ROTATIONS.seen: Every facing uses the same steel grey, thin round rails, gooseneck tops and outline. The south facing shows only the hooks, which is consistent with a ladder on the south wall face hidden from the camera. The 427% height spread is this real occlusion, not a size jump.

SIGNATURE.seen: A steel ladder with gooseneck rail tops curving over the rim, fixed to the pit wall. The raised state appears in the siblings and wall_context.

MATERIAL.seen: Dark steel with specular highlights on the round bars. It reads as metal tube.

FOOTPRINT.seen: In the pit composites each facing sits on its wall cell at a believable size. Nothing badly overflows.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha on all facings. Only a tight drop shadow sits along the bars; there is no backdrop or ground patch.

OURS.seen: A procedural redraw in the family's own style that matches the siblings. Not vanilla or another mod's art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: North now has thin rungs with open gaps, about 8 rungs that get closer together with depth, and rails that converge slightly. LEGIBLE.seen: At a drawSize of 1.5 the dark outlined rails and hooks still read as a ladder silhouette at 32 px per cell. Individual rungs will thin to about 1 px (see polish finding).

The port checklist is therefore satisfied, rather than unreadable or n/a. request.prompt: A single game sprite for RimWorld: a steel fire-escape-style ladder fixed to the wall of a dug pit, shown in the north-facing view. The view looks straight at the pit wall, face-on and orthographic, with the camera level and square to the wall. The ladder runs vertically down the center of the canvas, receding down into the pit. Two parallel vertical steel rails, riveted and slightly weathered, carry evenly spaced round rungs from the top of the canvas to the bottom. The rungs are slightly worn and lighter along their upper edges where they catch the light. The tops of both rails curve outward in a smooth gooseneck arc, curling over the rim of the pit at the top of the frame so the hooked ends read clearly. Small bolted standoff brackets hold the rails to the wall at regular intervals. Behind the ladder is a section of the pit wall: packed brown earth with a few embedded stones and subtle strata, getting slightly darker toward the bottom to suggest depth. The steel is cool grey-blue with scuffed highlights and a few rust streaks against the warm brown earth. Soft light falls from the upper left and gives a gentle cast shadow from the rails onto the wall. Painterly vanilla RimWorld art style, realistic hand-painted shading, clean dark outline around the ladder, rails and wall section. Transparent background outside the wall section. Square 384x384 canvas, the ladder centered and filling most of the frame. Single object, no text, no characters.
